::: {.hidden}

\newcommand{\sq}{\text{Sq}}
\newcommand{\pbc}{\mathcal{C_1}\times_{\mathcal{C_0}}\mathcal{C_1}}
\newcommand{\sw}{\text{swap}}
:::


# Definitions 


::: {#def-internal-graph}
## An internal graph in a category

\bigskip

Given a category $\mathbb{C}$, a [Graph Internal]{.underline} to $\mathbb{C}$ is a diagram

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0}
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", shift left=3, from=1-1, to=1-2]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

:::

::: {#def-internal-asynchronous-graph}
## An internal pre-asynchronous graph in a category

\bigskip

Given a category $\mathbb{C}$ with pullbacks, a [pre-Asynchronous Graph Internal]{.underline} to $\mathbb{C}$ is a diagram

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_1\times_{\mathcal{C}_0}\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0}
	\arrow["{\text{swap}}", from=1-1, to=1-1, loop, in=145, out=215, distance=10mm]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\ell}", shift left=3, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\pi_2}"', from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}", shift left=3, from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", shift left=3, from=1-3, to=1-4]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

satisfying the following equations written as commuting diagrams (using $\mathcal{C}_2 = \pbc$)
 
::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_2} & {\mathcal{C}_1} \\
	{\mathcal{C}_2} & {\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0}
	\arrow["\ell", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_2} & {\mathcal{C}_1} \\
	{\mathcal{C}_2} & {\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0}
	\arrow["\ell", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\pi_2}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_2}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::


::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{C}_2} & {\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_2} \\
	& {\text{Sq}}
	\arrow["\ell"', from=1-2, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\text{swap}}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}", curve={height=-6pt}, from=2-2, to=1-1]
	\arrow["\ell"', curve={height=6pt}, from=2-2, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

An Asynchronous graph internal to a category $\mathbb{C}$ is then defined as an octuple 
$A = (\sq, \mathcal{C}_1, \mathcal{C}_0, \sw, \ell, \mathfrak{r}, \text{src}, \text{tgt})$ with the additional property that $\ell$ is a 
monomorphism in $\mathbb{C}$.


::: 


::: {#thm-equivalent-defintions}

## Equivalent defintions of an Asynchronous Graph Internal to a Category

\bigskip

Let $A = (\sq, \mathcal{C}_1, \mathcal{C}_0, \sw, \ell, \mathfrak{r}, \text{src}, \text{tgt})$ be a pre-asynchronous graph internal to
$\mathbb{C}$. Suppose further that $\mathbb{C}$ has finite products then, the following are equivalent

 1. $A$ is an Asynchronous graph internal to $\mathbb{C}$;

 2. $\mathfrak{r}$ is a monomorphism; 

 3. $\langle \ell, \mathfrak{r}\rangle$ are jointly monic.


:::

::: {#prf-equivalent-definitions}

\bigskip

Exploit the triangle equatiosn to prove that $\sw$ is an involution of $\sq$ and then prove that $(1.)$ is equivalent to $(2.)$. It is then 
enough to show $(1.)$ implies $(3.)$.


:::





::: {#def-internal-graph-homomorphism}
## Internal graph homomorphism
An internal graph homomorphism is written internally to a category $\mathbb{C}$ like below: 


::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\bigg(\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0\bigg)} && {\bigg(\mathcal{C}'_1} & {\mathcal{C}'_0\bigg)}
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", shift left=3, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\qquad\quad graph}"', from=1-2, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}'}"', from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\text{src}'}", shift left=3, from=1-4, to=1-5]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

This means a pair of morphisms in $\mathbb{C}$, $f_0 : \mathcal{C}_0 \rightarrow \mathcal{C}'_0$ and 
$f_1 : \mathcal{C}_1 \rightarrow \mathcal{C}_1'$. The requirement on these morphisms is described by commutativity of both, the following, 
inside and outside squares to commute

::: {.imagify}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0} \\
	{\mathcal{C}_1'} & {\mathcal{C}_0'}
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", shift left=3, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{f_1}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{f_0}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\text{src}'}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}'}", shift left=3, from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}

:::


:::


::: {#def-asynchronous-graph-homomorphism}
## Internal asynchronous graph homomorphism
An internal asynchronous graph homomorphism is written internally to category $\mathbb{C}$ (with pullbacks) like below:

::: {.imagify}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\bigg(} & {\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_2} & {\mathcal{C}_1} & {\mathcal{C}_0\bigg)} \\
	\\
	{\bigg(} & {\text{Sq}'} & {\mathcal{C}_2'} & {\mathcal{C}_1'} & {\mathcal{C}_0'\bigg)}
	\arrow["{\text{swap}}"{description}, from=1-2, to=1-2, loop, in=145, out=215, distance=10mm]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}"', from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\ell", shift left=3, from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_2}"', from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}", shift left=3, from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["asynch"', from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}}"', from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\text{src}}", shift left=3, from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\text{swap}'}"{description}, from=3-2, to=3-2, loop, in=145, out=215, distance=10mm]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}'}"', from=3-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\ell'}", shift left=3, from=3-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_2}"', from=3-3, to=3-4]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}", shift left=3, from=3-3, to=3-4]
	\arrow["{\text{tgt}'}"', from=3-4, to=3-5]
	\arrow["{\text{src}'}", shift left=3, from=3-4, to=3-5]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

Similar to the internal graph homomorphism we have a pair of morphisms in $\mathbb{C}$, $f_0, f_1$ which extend to
$f_2 \triangleq f_1 \times_{f_0} f_1 : \mathcal{C}_2 \rightarrow \mathcal{C}_2'$. The morphisms $f_0$ and $f_1$ must satisfy the same 
commutative diagrams as for internal graph homomorphims. Furthermore, there is another morphism $f_{\text{sq}} : \sq \rightarrow \sq'$ 
which has a requirement on it to force the commutativity of, both of, the following (outter and innner) diagram(s):


::: {.imagify}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\text{Sq}} & {\mathcal{C}_2} \\
	{\text{Sq}'} & {\mathcal{C}'_2}
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\ell", shift left=3, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{f_{\text{sq}}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{f_2}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\ell'}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\mathfrak{r}'}", shift left=3, from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}

:::




:::
